requirements.limitation: The XMI count predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces ordered regular/decision-flow input types through prose:DecisionNode.input_types; unrepresented token types remain unsupported.
The XMI count predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces decisionInputFlow token-type conformance through prose:DecisionNode.input_types; unrepresented types remain unsupported.
The XMI count predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces the sole object input type through prose:DecisionNode.input_types; unrepresented types remain unsupported.

The XMI count/bounds predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces selection input/output types through prose:ObjectFlow.selection_types. Behavior purity remains an external evidence obligation.

The XMI count predicate is preserved. validate() additionally enforces upstream/input and output/downstream conformance through prose:ObjectFlow.transformation_types. Behavior purity remains an external evidence obligation.
Input/output counts, multiplicities and nominal type variance are checked (with a documented source-body correction). Absence of side effects of the selection Behavior is not proved.
Specific/general machine links are represented. Behavioral protocol-conformance proof is not implemented.
The model represents receiving/merged Package links. The normative reconciliation/merge algorithm is not implemented.

Strict availability views and checked creation support UML metaclass references, imported profiles, extended subtypes and conflicting filters. Direct constructors remain available for general model editing. Non-UML metaclasses need an adapter; UI presentation and CMOF interoperability remain open.

Runtime typed tags support effective inherited/redefined properties, literal defaults, bounds, readonly values, enumerations, profile Class/DataType objects, binary navigable inverses, composition and deletion. Model-defined primitive lexical values retain exact type identity; Python semantics require explicit per-definition codecs. User constraints use trusted Python callbacks or Boolean literals, never arbitrary OCL execution. Derived/general default evaluators, association-owned runtime navigation, full CMOF serialization and exhaustive profile semantics remain open.

The XMI predicate retains context-owned peer traversal. validate() additionally checks prose:Continuation.same_context_lifelines across the whole session, including nested owned Interactions sharing context. Literal selector values and selector identity are supported; distinct nonliteral selectors report unsupported rather than comparing absent value fields as equal. Arbitrary selector equivalence remains context dependent.

Trusted reference facts are checked against represented covered lifeline roles/types, interaction parameters/context attributes and read-only Properties. Full runtime ownership/global/write-once semantics remains a project approximation.
Trusted reference facts and represented read-only Properties are supported. Arbitrary domain global/write-once storage semantics is not represented by core UML and is not proved.
Trusted guard reference facts are checked against represented operand coverage/context. General domain-global and write-once facts remain incomplete.
Guard composite ownership is checked. Graphical placement immediately above a fragment requires UMLDI/layout semantics and is not proved.

The check uses represented ordered fragment containment with nested fragments visited before following siblings. A full partial-order semantics for parallel/alternative operands and GeneralOrdering is not implemented.

The XMI predicate is preserved, including vacuous direct values. validate() additionally enforces prose:Message.reply_argument_types on direct typed values, first expression operands and wildcards; arbitrary expression evaluation remains outside this check.

The XMI predicate retains the Artifact-only derivation. validate() additionally checks prose:DeploymentSpecification.configured_instance_elements using modeled Artifact instances. Nested-artifact and runtime-copy semantics remain open.

The XMI query retains its Artifact-only filter. The supplemental deployed_elements resolver expands direct manifestations of modeled Artifact classifiers/instances. Nested-artifact, inherited-manifestation, slot and runtime-copy semantics remain open.
